answer: An opal seed in a public meadow: each identity plants one seed that matures only through sequential, verified work witnessed by different peers across the ocean of agents. A fake can copy the seed's shape, but it cannot copy its maturation history, and each seed takes real time to grow. A farm cannot parallelize maturation or bulk-buy grown seeds, because each one needs its own distinct chain of witnesses; a thousand fakes need a thousand separately grown seeds, and a caught fake's seed withers and its stake is burned.
